name: Arthur Clifton
bio: A solicitor and friend of Wilde's from the 1880s, later a director of the Carfax Gallery. Seven of Wilde's letters to him survive. He was among the small number of people Wilde asked to dinner to meet other friends, and one of the letters is Wilde going over a poem of his line by line.
bio_note: SEVEN LETTERS at repo PDF 396, 404, 407, 432, 482, 483 and 537; TWO read at the page (printed 410 and 463, folios confirmed). DATES NOT RECORDED and none inferred.

sources.quote: My dear Arthur, The new last line 'Paradise' is charming. 'Vice' does not do as it is a word tainted in its signification with moral censure - vitium: what is faulty. The evening was charming. I enjoyed it all. Ever yours
sources.context: Wilde to Arthur Clifton, [postmark 28 January 1891], [16 Tite Street] (MS Clark) - quoted whole. Wilde is editing a poem of Clifton's and reaches for the Latin: vitium means a flaw or defect, and his argument is that the English word has been contaminated by moralising and no longer means what its root means.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: Wilde refusing the vocabulary of moral censure, in private, four years before it was used on him.
sources.provenance: Repo PDF page 483; printed folio 463 confirmed on the rendered page image.

sources.quote: Dear Arthur, Do you really wish to buy the necklace? £6 is a heap of money. Ever yours … I shall call at the Club (N. L.) tonight about 10.30 if I can. But write at once.
sources.context: Wilde to Arthur Clifton, [postmark 8 August 1889], 16 Tite Street (MS Private) - quoted whole including the postscript; the ellipsis marks only the signature falling mid-letter. The club is the National Liberal. Trivial in content and kept for the register: Wilde calling in at half past ten at night and wanting an answer the same day. ADDED 2026-08-05 during the page sweep - it was on a folio read for Kersley and not logged.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: The everyday footing of the friendship.
